#1688. HMRC chase the estate of late ex-England manager Sven-Goran Eriksson for £3.5MILLION in unpaid tax - because he was 'too busy with his ladies to save'

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 06:19 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 06:25 EST, 10 November 2026

Sven-Goran Eriksson's estate is being chased by HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) for an outstanding £3.5million in tax owed.

It comes as a result of the estate's inheritance following Eriksson's death in August 2024 due to pancreatic cancer.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport last year, the former England manager reportedly had assets worth £4.8m but owed a staggering £7.25m to HMRC alone. He also reportedly had at least £1m outstanding in other debts.

In a bid to help reduce that outstanding debt, his family sold his old mansion called Bjorkefors last year - albeit at a substantial loss.

Eriksson is survived by his son Johan, 47, and daughter Lina, 39 - from his first marriage to Ann-Christine Pettersson - as well as partner Yaniseth Alcides. During his time as England manager he had a high-profile relationship with Nancy Dell'Olio.

Speaking to The Sun, Eriksson's lawyer Anders Runebjer has revealed that the estate has no money left to settle the debt - aside from £300,000 in a UK bank and £1m in a Cayman Islands tax haven. He also stated his focus is now to salvage any money for Eriksson's two children after the ex-Three Lions boss had spent his finances around football and women.

Ex-England manager Sven-Goran Eriksson's estate is being chased for £3.5million by HMRC

In August 2024, he passed away at the age of 76 following a battle with pancreatic cancer

The Swede is survived by his two children Johan, 47, and daughter Lina, 39

'Sven earned millions but was always too busy with his football and his ladies to manage money very well,' said Runebjer.

'I told the HMRC I'm not able to get the money in the Cayman Islands or his UK bank and said they're welcome to seize it.

'They replied that they couldn't do that so I told them there was nothing else left - so they won't get paid.

'Sven was regularly sent bills by the British taxman and paid promptly but they changed the rules and now say he still owes £3.5m plus interest after he passed away.

'They're welcome to take whatever they can get but I'm not giving them anything.

'My priority is trying to get whatever money I can that he left for his children - not the British taxman.'

As aforementioned, Eriksson's estate sold his seven-bed house in Torsby, in his native Sweden - located on the banks of Lake Fryken - but at a reduced price.

According to The Sun, the property was on the market for £2m but his family had to lower the price by £400,000 to attract any prospective buyers.

And they went on to add that an anonymous e-commerce businesswoman has now bought it for an undisclosed sum of at least £1.3m - meaning a potential £700,000 loss on market value alone. However, the loss is greater as Eriksson bought the place in 2002 for £4.5m - meaning the true value lost is around £3m.

Last year, Eriksson's former home in Sweden was sold as his family look to reduce debt

Eriksson lived in the property with his partner Yaniseth Alcides until his death

During his time as England boss, he was in a high-profile relationship with Nancy Dell'Olio

Selling the property was the latest thing Eriksson's family have done in a bid to ease the financial burden they have taken on since his death.

In March 2025, they were forced to auction off his memorabilia - such as a lunch invitation from the late Queen.

Also up for auction was his Armani suit from a 2006 World Cup match with his hand-written team notes still in the pocket.

The 349 items reported to have gone under the hammer for a combined total of £140,000 also include his BBC Coach of the Year trophy in 2001 and a Premier League Manager of the Month award from his time as Manchester City boss.

An Ivory Coast top signed with a special message by former forward Didier Drogba from Eriksson's time as national coach in 2010 was sold as well.

Eriksson was estimated to have received around £7m in pay-offs alone from England, Manchester City and Mexico during his managerial career.

The Swede, who managed England between 2001 and 2006, previously described himself as being 'stupid' with his money.

In one of his last ever interviews, he told The Guardian: 'I was never interested in money - I never took care of it and trusted people to do that for me. I was stupid not to control where the money went. I realised that when I didn't have any more cash!

'I still don't know what I have in the bank.'

#1687. Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

Chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

Play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

Chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

Kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an important block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

Former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik

Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David

Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”

How long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

Looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck

Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap

The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

They have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Another new arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

Alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

#1686. Rabiot praises Donnarumma’s performance and admits France need time: “Part of the journey”

Last night, AC Milan’s Adrien Rabiot returned to San Siro – alongside Mike Maignan – as the French national team were beaten by Italy.

There was talk in the last international break that Zinedine Zidane wasn’t a huge fan of Rabiot. Yet, the midfielder was awarded the armband at San Siro. With this, a statement was made that the Frenchman needed to impress, but the trust was there for him to do so.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Whilst he could not lead his team to victory, though, there were several positives to take from the game, with one outlet giving him a 7/10.

It’s a frustrating defeat for Les Bleus – and a rare one for Rabiot and Maignan at San Siro – but it shows that they still have a lot to do with Zidane. After all, it’s better for these defeats to come now, rather than in a major tournament.

Speaking to Sky Sport (via MilanNews) after the game at San Siro, Rabiot praised the opposition goalkeeper – a remark made after an incredible save against him – as well as looking at where France stand after a few games under Zidane.

A leader of Milan and France. How much does this defeat weigh on the standings?

“It will be a tough game to play, the last one, because we need to win. The coach told us it’s part of the journey. We’re on a new path and we’re doing some things well, others a little less so. Tonight was a great game to watch.

“We did some very good things, but not so much in the second half. They showed a little more determination and deserved to win.”

“Donnarumma did well. We could have closed the game out in the first half because we were in a better position than them. In the second half, it was the opposite, even though he made two or three incredible saves. That’s part of football. They played a good game. They have strong, new players.

“It’s not easy, but I wish them the best because there’s a lot to do. It was an exciting match.”

#1685. Estonia vs Bulgaria - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 14 Nov 2026 23:32, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 02:37

Estonia will welcome Bulgaria to the Lillekula Stadium in Tallinn for Monday's UEFA Nations League encounter.

The hosts, who have secured a top-two finish, could still achieve automatic promotion, while the visitors only have pride to play for on the final matchday of the league phase.

Having been in the bottom two tiers for all five editions of the Nations League, Estonia have put themselves in a position to win promotion to League B for the very first time.

Jurgen Henn's side are guaranteed at least a promotion playoff spot after winning the draw and drawing three of their five matches in Group 4C.

In fact, they have recorded four consecutive shutouts since playing out a 1-1 draw with Iceland on the first matchday.

Their latest clean sheet enabled them to pick up a 1-0 victory in Saturday's away clash against Luxembourg, which came courtesy of Maksim Paskotsi's second goal of the 2026-27 Nations League campaign.

Sitting in second spot and two points adrift of Iceland, Estonia know they need a win and Luxembourg to claim three points in Reykjavik if they are to snatch automatic promotion on the final matchday.

That would require Estonia to pick up their first-ever win against Bulgaria, having drawn two and lost one of their previous three meetings.

Bulgaria already know they will be competing in League C next time around after falling hopelessly short in their promotion bid, mustering just four points from their five matches in Group C4.

After taking just a point from their first three games, Bulgaria finally ended their five-game winless run in all internationals with a 2-0 away victory over Luxembourg in their final outing of the September/October international break.

However, they failed to build upon that result in their most recent outing against Iceland, as they slumped to a demoralising 5-0 defeat in Plovdiv, ensuring they will end the league phase without a home win to their name.

While they cannot finish any higher than third, the Lions are still at risk of dropping to the bottom of the group, with just a point separating them from Luxembourg in fourth position.

Bulgaria may be unbeaten in three meetings against Estonia, but they had to settle for a goalless draw in their only previous away encounter in European Championship qualifying in April 2003.

Their hopes of troubling the scorers on this occasion may be tempered by the fact they have failed to score in three of their last four outings, including a stalemate in September's reverse fixture between these two nations.

Henn could opt for consistency by naming the same lineup that started Friday's narrow win over Luxembourg.

Friday's match-winner Paskotsi will feature alongside Erko Tougjas and Karol Mets in central defence, while Rasmus Peetson and Michael Schjonning-Larsen are set to operate as the two wing-backs.

At the opposite end of the pitch, Patrik Kristal will lead the line with Mattias Mannilaan, who is aiming to bring his club form to the international stage after netting five goals in his last four games for Kalju.

As for the visitors, they are unable to call upon Martin Minchev, who withdrew from the squad last week due to injury.

With Ribarski likely to make alterations, Ivan Turitsov and Dimitar Velkovski are in contention to feature in the backline on Monday.

Martin Petkov, Ivaylo Chochev and Georgi Lazarov are also among those who could come into Ribarski's thinking.

Hein; Peetson, Paskotsi, Tougjas, Mets, Schjonning-Larsen; Kait, Palumets, Shein; Mannilaan, Kristal

Naumov; Turitsov, Velkov, Tsenov, Velkovski; Kraev, Gruev; L Petkov, Chochev, M Petkov; Lazarov

Estonia have proven to be a tough team to break down in Group C4, and considering Bulgaria have failed to score in three of their last four games, we think the hosts could edge a cagey contest on Monday.

Matthew Montgomery, the science officer of a simulated Mars mission organized by NASA, takes part in a ‘Martian’ geology project.Credit: NASA

Engineer Matthew Montgomery was one of a four-person crew who spent more than a year in a 158-square-metre, 3D-printed habitat for a simulated mission on the red planet. The hardware-engineering design consultant (and co-owner of a film production company) took charge of the hydroponic garden and participated in simulated ‘Marswalks’ wearing a protective suit. As well as dealing with a realistic 13–22-minute delay in their connection with mission control, the crew experienced a total communication blackout for two weeks.

A new artificial-intelligence tool can identify an individual bird by its song, and can be used to track that bird’s movements over time. The system provides a less invasive way to monitor birds than using physical tags. Researchers tested the model on recordings of male ovenbirds (Seiurus aurocapilla) — a species that sings individually unique songs — from more than 100 locations, and found that it could match songs to specific birds with up to 96% accuracy. “This is almost a holy grail,” says biologist Scott Sillett.

The amount that preprint platform XSci pays referees for a quick-turnaround peer review. Authors pay up to $399 for a round of review. (Nature | 10 min read)

Protecting key underground fungal networks in Mongolia could help to preserve biodiversity, boost climate resilience and revive iconic grasslands across the country, say researchers. In September, evolutionary biologist Toby Kiers and her team announced that they had found more than 500 types of fungus in networks across Mongolia, 90% of which were new to science. Mycologist Burenjargal Otgonsuren hopes that leveraging these networks could help to restore the swathes of degraded land in Mongolia — and preserve the 3,000-year-old way of life practiced by Mongolia’s 230,000 nomadic herding families.

Sources: Free to Think 2026; V-Dem Dataset (https://go.nature.com/47UZF3P)

Academic freedom is deteriorating globally, according to the Scholars at Risk (SAR) network, a human-rights organization based at New York University. Data show a steep decline in academic freedom in the United States, some of which preceded the 2024 election of President Donald Trump. But there is cautious optimism about the trend in Hungary following the end of Viktor Orbán’s 16-year premiership.

By studying people who show no signs of neurodegeneration well into older age, scientists have identified several gene variants that could help to protect against dementia. These protective variants seem to defend the brain against the toxic clusters of proteins that cause Alzheimer’s — mechanisms that scientists now hope to exploit. “Nature has already done the experiment for us: certain gene variants protect us from Alzheimer’s,” says neuroscientist Guojun Bu. “Learning how they do this could guide us to new therapies.”

The mathematics community’s reaction to OpenAI’s huge drop of AI-generated proofs last month “ranged from exhilaration to despair”, writes mathematician Ursula Martin, one of the authors of the Leiden Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics, which put forward several safeguards on the technology. “This is a moment to be clear-eyed about AI’s potential to make discoveries,” she writes. “The challenge … is to sustain the community of mathematicians on whom the discipline depends.”

Reference: Leiden Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics

Biomining strategies — those that use microorganisms to extract metals — could provide a more sustainable alternative to conventional technologies, which are struggling to keep up with soaring demand for critical minerals, argue a group of biotechnology and mining researchers. These methods can also extract metals from discarded electronics, reducing the need for virgin ores. For biomining methods to reach their potential, researchers must work with governments and industry to establish a pathway through which these technologies can be deployed at scale, the authors write.

The NASA space probe Voyager 1 is now almost one light-day away from Earth. Nearly 50 years after its launch, finding ways to conserve power on the spacecraft requires innovative thinking, says heliophysicist Jamie Rankin, deputy project scientist of the Voyager mission. #1683. ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

“We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments but the compete part – especially in and around our box – was not to the standards to win a football match against a good side. It’s better to give them [the goals away] in a friendly match than an official match. It’s always good when you lose a match in pre-season because it creates a bit more fire in the belly.”

Kepa Arrizabalaga will not want to watch Betis’s first goal back in a hurry. The Arsenal goalkeeper may have got a slight nudge as he came for the ball at a corner but he was all over the place and never looked even in the vaguest control of the situation. Rodrigo Riquelme scored at the far post after the ball sailed over the keeper. Arteta called it a “really sloppy goal”. With former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier having arrived on a free transfer as back-up to Raya, Kepa faces an uncertain future at Arsenal. Moments like this will not help his cause.

He did not feature much last season but is probably best remembered for his torrid showing in the Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City in March. He looked as unconvincing here as he did then, as the former Chelsea goalkeeper also sliced a clearance in the build up to Betis’s third goal. Before then, Kai Havertz had turned over possession cheaply from which Nelson Deossa set up former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals to score.

Arsenal need more creativity and firepower in attack, hence the interest in Vinícius and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez. Viktor Gyokeres again looked rather limited here and the likes of Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze are also still to report back. Yet one of the few, brighter aspects of Arsenal’s performances was the sight of the regal looking Riccardo Calafiori marauding forward from a very nominal left-back role.

If Arsenal are going to play more adventurously this season and try to ratchet up things in the entertainment stakes then Calafiori could have a big role to play, as long as Arteta can keep him fit. He can be a potent weapon galloping forward and there were clear glimpses of that here. Harnessing that talent while not compromising too much defensive security may be one of the manager’s challenges.

Louie Copley had only been on the pitch for nine minutes – a half-time substitute for Ben White – when the 19-year-old midfielder went down largely unchallenged with what looked like a troubling knee injury. Arteta admitted afterwards that the way the teenager fell to the ground was a concern and he looked in visible pain and distress as he was treated by the medical staff before being helped off the pitch.

The fear will be of some kind of ligament damage and Arteta confirmed Copley would be scanned on Thursday. “Quite worried to be fair for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive and the symptoms that he already has,” the manager said. “So we are going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. Touch wood that is not a bad one.”

“It is another opportunity for fitness. Coming into games against teams of good quality, it is important we get good fitness. It is a chance to build momentum for the season ahead. We are taking steps in the right direction. Of course, we want more from the performance and the results, but we take learnings and move on.

“All of us, together, we share a common goal. We have confidence to build on. We will take every game as it comes. The atmosphere was amazing. I did not realise Ireland has so many Arsenal fans. Isco should put Betis 4-1 up but tries to be too cute and clever. Former Arsenal man Bellerin delivers a cross from the right side of the box and picks out a free Isco in the six-yard box. Isco attempts an audacious flick rather than putting his foot through it and his effort is saved by Meslier. That should have been a goal.

Arsenal have changed nearly their entire starting XI whereas Betis have made just the one substitution thus far. Betis have played more games so far in pre-season, which probably explains the difference in the number of changes.

Salmon is deceived by a dummy by Riquelme and then brings the Betis man down, earning him a yellow card.

On the hour mark, Mikel Arteta is going to make a triple change, which feels like it was a plan going into the game. That includes Meslier coming on in goal in place of Kepa.

Copley is helped off by the two Arsenal medics, shaking his head and not putting any weight on his left leg, and is replaced by Julienne.

You have to hope that the knee injury to Louie Copley is not serious but judging by the way he went down largely unchallenged, his reaction and the way he was being helped down the tunnel it didn’t look too good. A tough moment for the youngster who had only been on the pitch nine minutes.

Play is halted as Copley has been down for a little while clutching at his left knee. He got his studs stuck in the ground and went down in some pain. The medics come on to check that left knee. He only came on at half-time but his night is over not even 10 minutes into the second half.

Nwaneri catches Bernal and if this was a competitive fixture than I think Nwaneri would perhaps have been booked for that challenge.

Those raft of changes from Mikel Arteta at half-time have seen just four of their starting XI remain on the pitch; Kepa, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly and Nwaneri.

Arsenal have a corner early on in this second half as Vieira’s shot from distance deflects behind. The delivery from the left has too much on it, going over the heads of all the Arsenal players in the box, and Betis are able to clear.

Mikel Arteta has made a whole host of changes, which includes the likes of Jesus, Martinelli, Gabriel and Vieira coming on. Betis have brought the former Real Madrid man Isco on at the break.

Arsenal’s title triumph was built on that stout defence and conceding so few but there have been so many self-inflicted wounds here. The first half is brought to an end and Real Betis take a 3-1 lead into the break.

Manuel Pellegrini’s side have their third goal of the night and restore their two-goal advantage. Havertz gives the ball away poorly deep inside his own half and the ball is played into Fornals. The former West Ham man has it on the edge of the box and has P Garcia in space to his right but opts to shoot. It is a clinical finish from Fornals as he picks out the bottom left corner and celebrates by crossing his arms to form irons, paying tribute to his days at West Ham.

Betis have one goal from a corner and now Arsenal do. Betis keeper Valles complains that he is being fouled by Havertz after Tzolis swung in the corner from the left and the ball comes through to Hincapie, who has the simplest of headers from inside the six-yard box.

Since Gyokeres misses that very good chance just a minute into the game, Arsenal have not really carved out many genuine opportunities in front of goal, other than that Tzolis wasted chance. Every time they reach the final third, they are lacking that cutting edge.

Calafiori’s role is interesting. He’s very nominally a left back but is routinely stepping into midfield and raiding forward, often ending up in positions you’d associate with a No. 10. It’s the kind of role Nico O’Reilly played under Pep Guardiola at Manchester City.

Valles is so, so lucky. The Betis keeper inexplicably passes the ball straight at Tzolis inside the Betis penalty area but Tzolis is unable to capitalise. That is a huge slice of luck for Valles as that was a ridiculous moment.

Betis have already scored one goal from a corner and they now have another corner after Nwaneri’s clearance behind. The inswinger is sent into a good area but this time Arsenal deal with the danger.

Arsenal were the better side in the early stages but Betis have grown into this and have taken confidence from that goal.

Calafiori may be on the teamsheet tonight for Arsenal at left-back but when they are in possession the Italian is moving into midfield. Lewis-Skelly, who is playing in the number six role, is dropping in between the two centre-backs when Arsenal have the ball.

Betis win a free-kick out on the left, with the chance to send it into the Arsenal penalty area for the first time tonight. It is clipped into a good area but Kepa is out of his goal to catch it.

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Spanish side Real Betis at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, with this being the first-ever meeting between the two sides. This is the first time Arsenal have played a pre-season game in Dublin since August 2018, when they drew 1-1 with London rivals Chelsea, with Arsenal winning on penalties.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 in their opening game of pre-season, with new signing Christos Tzolis on the scoresheet in his first appearance for the club. After today, Arsenal have three more games, including the Community Shield, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry on opening night of the new season. They are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to become one of Arsenal’s most expensive signings. Mikel Arteta’s side have been dealt a blow ahead of the season with the news that France centre-back William Saliba will miss an extended period due to a back injury. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Real Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, finished fifth in La Liga last season and have therefore qualified for this coming season’s Champions League after a 20-year absence from the competition. Pellegrini has led Betis into European competitions for five consecutive seasons, which includes losing the 2025 Europa Conference League final to Chelsea. They have been busy in pre-season action already having played five games up to this point. They have won four of the five, including a 4-0 victory over Lyon, with just one defeat coming against Granada.

They have a number of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Antony, Giovani Lo Celso, Pablo Fornals and former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin. Real Betis have already played a number of friendlies as they build up to the start of their season, which begins on August 21 when they take on Real Sociedad.

#1682. MN: Tomori could return against Frosinone with check-up scheduled next week

Fikayo Tomori suffered a thigh tear against Bologna, and AC Milan are awaiting updates about his recovery. However, some good news has arrived.

The international break couldn’t have come at a better time for Tomori. It allows him to recover at Milanello without missing valuable training time with the team. Given 13 players have been called up this week, he’s hardly in a ‘proper’ environment currently.

So, it allows him the chance to work and potentially return at the same time as many of his teammates.

This morning, MilanNews have provided an update on Tomori’s injury, with the defender working at Milanello on recovery. In fact, he’s progressing well and ‘important news’ regarding his return is expected in the upcoming days.

Another check-up is scheduled for early next week to assess the progress of the injury recovery, and if that goes smoothly, he could begin training on the pitch again. It is possible, therefore, that he could be back on the pitch against Frosinone on November 22.

Given the shortness at the back, Ruben Amorim will have to balance the need to have him back and his ability to offer minutes. He can’t be rushed back, especially with the risk of worsening the injury.

#1681. Liverpool transfer news: 'Significant' interest in £29m centre-back as Andoni Iraola ponders future without Virgil van Dijk

By Lewis Nolan | 14 Nov 2026 23:43, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 01:33

Liverpool are keen on Lens centre-back Pierre Ismaelo Ganiou despite interest from a number of other clubs, the latest report has claimed.

The Premier League is now on pause for the November international break, and that has given Reds supporters the chance to assess the squad.

Andoni Iraola has made a positive start to life at Anfield, with the team's defence having notably improved, led by the likes of Virgil van Dijk and Ronald Araujo.

However, Van Djik has entered the final year of his contract, while Araujo is only on loan from Barcelona and could return to the Spanish side at the end of the season.

Amid uncertainty regarding the future of their defence, Football Insider report that the Reds are one of several clubs keen on signing Lens defender Ganiou, who is valued by Transfermarkt at just over £25m.

Ganiou does not have an extensive history of top-flight football considering he has played just 28 games in Ligue 1 in his entire career, though he has been impressive for Lens.

In five league matches for the French side this season, the 21-year-old has won 69% of his duels, including 73% of his ground duels.

Liverpool have typically looked to sign aerially dominant defenders, so while the Frenchman boasts an impressive 64% duel success rate in the air, he only averages 1.8 aerial duels won per game.

Van Dijk has won an average of 3.8 duels in the air in the league so far, while Jeremy Jacquet has won 2.6 aerial duels in the Premier League, and the Reds would almost certainly aim to get Ganiou closer to those figures.

While Van Dijk is 35 and is into the final year of his contract, he has shown no signs of physical decline, and he has expressed a desire to remain at Anfield.

If he was to extend his stay on Merseyside, the Reds may not need to delve into the market for another centre-back.

Joe Gomez is expected to leave, and he could be replaced in the squad by Araujo, which would then leave the club in need of a right-back.

Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni will be part of the squad for the coming seasons, while many believe that Ifeanyi Ndukwe could play a role for the team once his loan at Levante ends.

#1680. What Man United, with their seemingly addictive habit, must do now once Michael Carrick is sacked: IAN LADYMAN on Sir Jim Ratcliffe's trail of bad judgment and waste

Published: 02:00 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 07:53 EST, 10 November 2026

Those who were there will never forget the utter chaos of Michael Carrick’s last act at Old Trafford. But as the outgoing United manager clung on to his dignity like a life raft in those mad closing moments against Aston Villa, the current poster boy for United’s desperate demise sat on the bench in his tracksuit.

Diogo Dalot is an honest and by all accounts fully committed Portuguese full-back who has been a United player for more than eight years.

The 27-year-old was bought for his teenage potential by his compatriot Jose Mourinho in 2018 but has never trained on. He has never been good enough for a really top English club yet has made more than 250 appearances for the most famous one of all and has played for five different permanent managers.

On Sunday he was booed off by his own supporters when substituted after an hour. His had been a particularly grim performance but the boos were not about him, not really.

No they were not about Dalot but instead about the fundamental truth of what he represents. Namely a steady, grisly and unforgivable drain of footballing standards at United that actually began in the final days of Sir Alex Ferguson and has subsequently never stopped.

It is this that has taken United from Ferguson’s final valedictory title of 2013 to where they are today, the bottom three of the Premier League. It is this that has drained United of all their clout and reputation. It is this that has cost yet another United manager – a seventh – his job.

Diogo Dalot has become the poster boy for the decline under Michael Carrick as Man United seemingly plumb new depths

The outgoing club legend is not a good enough manager for United and his appointment was yet another mis-step by the club's hierarchy

Carrick is not a good enough manager for United. His appointment was an emotional mistake, one of many made by Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the band of misfits and hopefuls who are currently in charge of football operations.

With a better manager – a better coach – in charge of the current team, United would be in the top half of the league. The fact they sit 18th and resemble a Sunday League team that never gets going until they have shaken their hangovers off is squarely down to him.

Nevertheless, United are a football club that exists to win trophies, no matter what the majority owners the Glazers may have said recently. But United will not win the big trophies again until they buy better players and by that I mean better footballers and better people.

It sounds simple, trite even. But it’s a simple truth of our game. Until United can reverse a seemingly addictive habit of paying too much money for too little, the difference made by a manager will only ever be a matter of six or seven places in the Premier League standings. And United needs a much greater improvement than that until this vicious cycle of self-harm comes to an end.

There is so much wrong at the modern Manchester United away from the field. Much of it begins and ends with the hideous hubris and self-regard of Ratcliffe, a man so shot through with misplaced self-confidence that he still insists on being tailed everywhere by a journalist he has hired to write a book on United’s journey back to the top of the mountain. Suffice to say that one won’t be ready for this Christmas.

But the thread that links the final days of Ferguson and his chief executive David Gill through the years of Ed Woodward, Richard Arnold and John Murtough to these dark days of Ratcliffe’s INEOS control is simple. It’s sub-standard players.

Despite the financial drain of the Glazers’ stranglehold, United have spent in the region of £1.75bn on their first team in the last ten years.

It takes quite something to do that and take a club backwards. It takes quite something to do that and buy only one player – captain Bruno Fernandes – who can claim to have been consistently effective over his time at the club.

Somehow, though, United have managed it and it is this hideous trail of bad judgment and waste that follows the current team and those that have come before it every time it runs out on to the field.

United are weak off the pitch and even weaker on it. Their football mirrors their off-field strategy. Haphazard, wasteful and inconsistent.

A number of years ago – at a time when previous CEOs Woodward and Arnold were trying to mend a broken club - they enlisted the advice of Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton and former captain Bryan Robson to help them work out what exactly a United team should be.

‘Exciting, daring, confident and humble’ were the key words they laid down. Well, what on earth happened to any of that?

United have a huge decision to make – yet again – over a new manager. The field of suitable candidates is not as big as they would like. Nor is United as attractive a proposition as it was. The demands are enormous yet the foundations shake. It’s not a good combination.

A good coach would improve them. Carrick has had two central defenders on his staff in Jonny Evans and Jonathan Woodgate. What on earth have they been doing for the last two or three months?

Long before the arrival of Jim Ratcliffe former chief executive Ed Woodward and Richard Arnold attempted to draw a blueprint for the club

Their successors in the boardroom Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have not impressed over a baffling summer

But United remain four or five good transfer windows away from where they need to be and the last time they put a run of good business like that together at Old Trafford Carrick was probably in the first team.

United need proper talent but they also need proper people, not the kind who would rather moan to TV cameras after a defeat than go home and think about their own part in what has just happened.

Last summer’s strategy seemed to have come straight out of Chat GPT and reflects terribly on the current football director Jason Wilcox. To ‘fix’ the midfield through three signings with the need to ‘fix’ the back four kicked down the road for 12 months is not so much a strategy as an exercise in transfer suicide.

Some think Wilcox should follow Carrick through the door on the back of that and it’s a reasonable point of view. Viewed through the mist of an autumn afternoon on Sunday, Wilcox looked as grey as his recent track record. An alternative take is that the recruitment of players like Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha is indicative of an uptick in returns, at least in part.

Whichever path you wish to walk, it simply has to lead to an improvement in the one area that will either nourish or starve a football club. With that in mind, the first question a prospective manager should ask is who is buying the players and on the back of what long-term strategy.

Carrick’s United team have looked like exactly what they are this season, a group put together by different people following different principles for different managers. How strange that it hasn’t worked.

United, as we know, needed a left-back over the summer. Lewis Hall, of England and Newcastle, may have been an option. Instead, United placed their faith in Luke Shaw, a 31-year-old with a long history of injuries.

Shaw, unsurprisingly, is currently injured which brings us back to where we started, namely the sight of the right-footed Dalot labouring out of position on the left of Carrick’s back four against Villa on Sunday.

You could say we saw this coming. Many did. In the dressing room and in the stands at Old Trafford. Carrick? He knew about it, too, but then he was only the manager.

His exit will hurt for a while. He is an emotionally intelligent and empathetic individual who will reel from the trauma of the last ten weeks. Over time he will realise that he is well out if it, though. When he took the job last summer, Ferguson is known to have been concerned about what it may do to him. As often, Carrick’s old boss was right.

United are set up to fail and Carrick’s replacement will realise that soon enough. When he walks into the first team dressing room for the first time and looks for those upon whom he can rely to consistently help him, too many eyes will be focussed on the floor.

#1679. De Rossi admits Genoa ‘lost well’ to Milan and recalls Moreira’s comment: “Even our opponents notice”

Daniele De Rossi has looked back at Genoa’s defeat to AC Milan and how he wasn’t frustrated with his team afterwards.

Milan entered the international break with a much-needed victory against Genoa, but it wasn’t the easiest result of the season. After a disappointing defeat to Ferencvaros – which extended the midweek run of defeats – they couldn’t afford to drop points, and they succeeded, even if it wasn’t without flaw.

With two goals inside 20 minutes, you’d be forgiven for expecting Milan to win by more than a couple. However, that was the end of their goalscoring for the afternoon and although Genoa pulled one back, they didn’t grab more than a consolation goal.

Speaking to Sky Sport – in the new series ‘Radici’ – De Rossi looked back on the defeat to the Rossoneri, as well as a comment that stuck with him from Diego Moreira, as MilanPress have relayed today.

We indeed lost against Milan, but we lost ‘well.’ We didn’t deserve it. Three or four weeks ago, the latest results seemed like a pipe dream. I thank the players, staff, and my club for giving me faith and patience at a time when other clubs wouldn’t have had it.

“They remembered how good we did last year. I’m happy to have emerged from a difficult period and to be Genoa’s coach; I’m really happy there.”

“I’m passionate about the fans and the supporters. I’m part of a club that, in terms of fan base, is among the best in Europe. I’m passionate; I don’t punch a clock. I spend two hours with the stockman or the waitress with the same enthusiasm I spend time with the team captain. Experiencing it like that, you realise that Genoa is a great team.

“Genoa is full of Genoese fans who remind you every second how much they love their club, the pride of being the top club in Italy. The architecture of the stadium and the warmth of the fans… I’m not saying this to be a sycophant, but on Sunday Moreira came to me and said, ‘I’ve never seen anything like this here in Italy.’ It’s a reality that even our opponents notice.”

#1678. Germany vs Netherlands - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 14 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 04:46

Fighting for a place in the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals, Germany are set to host League A's Group A2 leaders, the Netherlands, at Olympiastadion Berlin on Monday.

Die Mannschaft know that they likely need to win to progress, while Oranje are through barring an unprecedented swing in goal-difference.

Jurgen Klopp's Germany are pushing to qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals for just the second time, but they face a tough test to reach the last eight.

Die Mannschaft are currently third in Group A2, level on eight points with Greece and three behind the Netherlands, and their chance to go through leans on the fact UEFA prioritises head-to-head points between tied teams.

Klopp's side were beaten 1-0 by the Azure and White on September 27 before drawing 0-0 with them on matchday four.

However, Ivan Jovanovic's men were hammered 7-0 by the Dutch on Friday, meaning that a German victory over the Netherlands on Monday would see them progress ahead of Greece regardless of their result against Serbia.

Die Mannschaft were held to a 1-1 stalemate by Oranje on matchday one, with Cody Gakpo equalising in second-half stoppage time to deny his former Liverpool manager maximum points.

Klopp's team have remained undefeated in the group since their loss to Greece, most recently beating Serbia 3-1 on Friday, when they raced into a 2-0 lead within the first 14 minutes thanks to an own-goal from Srdjan Babic and a follow-up by Florian Wirtz.

Meanwhile, Xavi's Netherlands have yet to taste defeat in the Nations League this term, and are in a commanding position at the top of their group going into the final matchday.

Leading with 11 points, Oranje's 7-0 demolition of Greece last time out - following a 2-2 draw on October 1 - means the only possibility of them finishing below the top two is if there is a dramatic 14-goal swing in the Azure and White's favour.

Xavi is without talismanic centre-back Virgil van Dijk this month, but his team were still able to keep their first clean sheet in the competition on Friday, while Tijani Reijnders's first-half hat-trick set the tone at the opposite end of the pitch.

However, it remains to be seen whether the Netherlands can repeat that attacking showcase in Germany, considering that they have won just one of their last six away clashes against Die Mannschaft.

On the other hand, Oranje are unbeaten in their past seven matches on the road, and last suffered a travelling defeat in a penalty shootout against Spain during the Nations League quarter-finals in March 2025, following a 5-5 aggregate draw.

Germany have no new injury issues to contend with, though they are missing Bayern Munich stars Jamal Musiala and Serge Gnabry due to respective muscle problems.

In their absence, Klopp could continue with Brajan Gruda, Florian Wirtz and Derry Scherhant behind Arsenal man Kai Havertz up top.

As for the Netherlands, they were forced to take off Frenkie De Jong at half time against Greece after he suffered back pain, and he has now left the national squad to return to Barcelona.

Teun Koopmeiners looks set to step in and fill the gap alongside Joey Veerman at the base of Xavi's midfield, while Tijani Reijnders operates in the number 10 role.

Further forward, Donyell Malen has been a standout for Roma this season with 12 goals across all competitions, and he will be keen to add to his goal against Greece while Cody Gakpo and Crysencio Summerville provide width.

Captain Virgil van Dijk has sat out this international break with complaints of physical discomfort, so expect to see Tottenham Hotspur's Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke start at centre-back.

Ter Stegen; Treu, Thiaw, Tah, Mittelstadt; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Gruda, Wirtz, Scherhant; Havertz

Verbruggen; Dumfries, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Timber; Veerman, Koopmeiners; Summerville, Reijnders, Gakpo; Malen

The maths of the table may be complex, but Germany know that a simple victory will see them through to the quarter-finals.

Oranje have yet to lose in the Nations League this season, though with the stakes lowered, they could be caught off guard.

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

Stepping up in the big moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR

Aston Villa’s preparations for the new season continue out in Hong Kong as they take on Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium. These sides have met twice before; Aston Villa beat Bayern 1-0 to win the European Cup in 1981/82 before then meeting in the Champions League group stages during the 2024/25 season, with Jhon Duran’s long-range screamer giving Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Villa Park.

After losing two of their first three pre-season friendlies, Aston Villa have won their first two games on Asian soil and this game marks the end of their tour of the Far East. It has been a summer of significant change at Aston Villa thus far with some key members of their squad departing and some new faces arriving. Youri Tielemans has departed after Manchester United triggered his release clause and they then sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for a British transfer record £117m. Unai Emery’s side have brought in 20-year-old Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi, Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes and Alejandro Garnacho, with the deal for Garnacho being an initial loan. Manzambi is currently on the sidelines due to a knee injury.

Unai Emery’s side were dealt a blow during the World Cup as Belgian midfielder Amadou Onana picked up a serious knee injury. They were though boosted by the return of Boubacar Kamara after seven months out as he scored in the 3-1 friendly victory over BG Parthum. As one midfielder returned from injury in that game, another picked up a fresh injury as John McGinn suffered a knock to his knee. The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return after their world Cup exploits. They begin their Premier League campaign with an away game on the south coast against Brighton on August 23 but will be involved in the Uefa Super Cup against PSG next week having lifted the Europa League last season.

Bayern Munich head into this season looking to win a third straight Bundesliga title and have won two of their three friendlies, losing once. They have added Moroccan attacker Ismael Saibari from PSV and German left-back Nathaniel Brown from Bundesliga rivals Eintracht Frankfurt to their ranks this summer. The likes of Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano and Michael Olise are not available as they are still yet to return after World Cup duty but Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Bayern’s German stars are set to return.

After today, Bayern have one more friendly against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

#1676. GdS: Linear structure and a strong work force – what Krösche is likely to implement at Milan

AC Milan are expected to hire Markus Krösche in the next few weeks, and a report has looked a little more at his work today.

Between Eintracht Frankfurt and Milan, there are plenty of differences. From the finances available to how they’re spent, even to the way in which the structure of the club ticks over. So, Krösche will have to learn with the Rossoneri.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, it won’t be a one way street, with the Diavolo needing to learn plenty too.

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, Krösche methods are very linear; it’s about arriving and leaving at the right time, having the knowledge to enter and the courage to step away when the time is right.

His belief is that the club will always hold more weight than the manager, which has been shown in the past few months by Gerry Cardinale and there is no shortage of exciting signings on his CV.

What is also worth remembering is that he’s not one to step away from his methods. In 2022, he was given a chance to sign Cristiano Ronaldo. However, it didn’t make sense for him or Frankfurt, so they never made their move.

If it happens his way, Timmo Hardung will arrive alongside the German. The pair met at RB Leipzig and their relationship has only grown since then and Krösche eventually led a team of 70 people at Frankfurt. In other words, he won’t be out of place at the top of the Milan football organisation.

Gazzetta even suggests that it’s ‘no secret’ that his desire is to move to Italy to work under Krösche once again. Given their successes together, it makes sense why all parties are hoping to keep that relationship under the same roof.

#1675. Central African Republic vs Benin - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 14 Nov 2026 23:59

Central African Republic host Benin at the Japoma Stadium in Douala, Cameroon, on Monday in the fourth round of Group F in 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying.

Benin won the first leg 4-1 in Abidjan on Thursday and lead Group F on goal difference, level on seven points with Burkina Faso, while Central African Republic remain bottom with no points and a goal difference of -6.

Central African Republic, known as Les Fauves, have lost all three qualifiers, scoring two goals and conceding eight, and have not won any match since October last year.

Mauritania won 3-1 in their opener on September 24, and Burkina Faso followed with a 1-0 victory over them on September 28.

Head coach Abdelaziz Kerkache, a Moroccan who has previously worked at Mouloudia d’Oujda, was appointed on November 6 to replace Eloge Enza Yamissi, only six days before the first leg.

Kerkache recalled Geoffrey Kondogbia of Olympique de Marseille and Le Mans forward Louis Mafouta, who both missed the opening two qualifiers, and Mafouta responded by equalising in the first leg.

Les Fauves had more of the ball in Abidjan, with 56% possession and eight corners to Benin’s five, yet goalkeeper Dominique Youfeigane faced eight shots on target and conceded four.

Central African Republic are still chasing a first Africa Cup of Nations finals appearance after narrowly missing out in 2021 and 2023, and their home leg is being staged in Douala rather than in Bangui.

Benin, nicknamed Les Guepards, have taken seven points from three Group F games under Gernot Rohr, beginning with a 1-1 draw at Burkina Faso on September 25.

A 2-1 win over Mauritania in Abidjan on September 29 followed, with Rodolfo Aloko scoring either side of half time, as Benin again used an Ivory Coast venue because the Stade de l’Amitie in Cotonou is not yet approved for qualifiers.

Hassane Imourane opened the scoring in the seventh minute of the first leg, Louis Mafouta equalised in the 19th, and Benin were 3-1 up at half time after Aloko struck in the 31st minute and Aiyegun Tosin in the 36th.

Tosin completed his brace in the 56th minute, and he and Aloko have now scored six of Benin’s seven goals in qualifying.

Benin won despite having only 44% of the possession, turning 18 shots into four goals, with eight efforts on target against Central African Republic’s 14 shots and five on target.

Rohr said afterwards that the scoreline flattered his side because Central African Republic attacked a great deal, and he expects a reaction in a rematch only four days later.

Kondogbia, Mafouta and Goduine Koyalipou all started in Abidjan, and Kerkache has had only one match to work with that group.

For Benin, captain and striker Steve Mounie remains out injured, so Rohr again leans on Aloko, Tosin and Junior Olaitan, who has three goals and seven assists for Besiktas this season.

Central African Republic have conceded eight goals in three qualifiers, and a second game in four days under Kerkache is unlikely to repair a defence that let in three before half time on Thursday.

#1674. California votes to give record $8.4 billion to medical research

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Students, researchers and others at the University of California, Los Angeles, have protested over cuts to science funding made by the administration of US President Donald Trump during the past two years.Credit: Robyn Beck/AFP via Getty

Voters in California have approved US$8.4 billion in funding for immunology research — the largest ever infusion of cash for science authorized by a public vote in US history.

The funding proposal, known as Proposition 38, appeared on the ballot for voters in California in last week’s US mid-term elections, but it has taken nearly a week for officials to count enough ballots to declare it a success. The state government will pay for the research — which aims to find treatments that harness or re-engineer the body’s immune system to fight illnesses such as cancer and Alzheimer’s disease — by selling state government bonds. (This is unusual for science funding. Bonds are typically reserved to pay for infrastructure projects such as road construction and require the state to pay back its debt with interest.)

‘Historic change’: what the 2026 US mid-term election results mean for science

‘Historic change’: what the 2026 US mid-term election results mean for science

Supporters of the proposal say that the funding will provide stability for researchers in California, who have been affected by political turmoil. The administration of US President Donald Trump has pushed for massive cuts to science funding; put political appointees in charge of grant decisions at federal science agencies such as the US National Institutes of Health; and forced policy change at US universities that receive federal funding, including those in California.

The $8.4 billion “is an advantage to California that is unprecedented”, says Antoni Ribas, a cancer researcher and physician at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), who supported Proposition 38. It will make the state “even more of a global hub for immunology research”.

But the proposal has sparked debate. That’s because it calls for about half of the funding to be given directly to research institutes — and the only institute that matches the criteria called for in the proposal is one co-founded by Gary Michelson, a billionaire medical-device inventor. He wrote the proposition and donated about $45 million of his own funds to get it placed on the ballot and to campaign for its passage.

“I feel like the voters have been taken advantage of,” says Sarah Hill, a political scientist at California State University in Fullerton, who tracks the state’s ballot measures. Michelson did not respond to Nature’s request for comment before this story was published, but has said elsewhere that he will not personally profit from the bond revenue.

In California, citizens can place proposed laws directly on the election ballot by collecting hundreds of thousands of voter signatures.

The state has funded scientific research through this process before. In 2004, after then president George W. Bush restricted federal funding for human embryonic stem-cell research, voters in California approved a $3-billion bond to establish the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine, which they then voted to replenish with another $5.5 billion in 2020.

A campaign mailer encouraging California voters to support Proposition 38.Credit: Smith Collection/Gado/Getty

“The model works,” Ribas says. Immunologists have been making great strides with medicines such as personalized treatments called CAR-T therapies, which are revolutionizing care, he says. There has also been a flurry of research into developing vaccines, including the mRNA shots that have been the target of funding cuts by the Trump administration. Proposition 38 will ensure that such research can continue regardless of the political headwinds, Ribas adds.

Around $4 billion from Proposition 38 will fund grants for researchers at select public universities and non-profit institutes in California through a competitive review process. According to the proposal, any commercialized therapies developed through funded research must be sold at a 20% discount to people in California, with 10% of drug royalties returning to the state’s general fund.

#1673. Iceland vs Luxembourg - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 15 Nov 2026 00:03, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 03:16

Iceland will look to wrap up automatic promotion when they welcome Luxembourg to Reykjavik for Monday's Nations League encounter.

The hosts are sitting two points at the top of Group C4, while the visitors are languishing at the bottom of the standings ahead of the final matchday of the league phase.

After being relegated from League B in 2024-25, Iceland have put in a strong performance in their first-ever League C campaign, collecting 11 points from a possible 15.

After playing out a 1-1 draw with Estonia, Arnar Gunnlaugsson's side recorded back-to-back 3-0 victories over Luxembourg and Bulgaria.

However, their momentum was somewhat halted by a goalless draw against Estonia in their final outing of the September/October international break.

But they certainly had no issues troubling the scorers in Friday's emphatic 5-0 away win over Iceland, which came courtesy of an Andri Gudjohnsen hat-trick, an Orri Oskarsson effort and an own goal.

Gudjohnsen, who is now the leading scorer in League C with five goals, has helped his country secure a playoff berth and put them in pole position to secure automatic promotion on the final matchday.

With a two-point advantage over Estonia, Iceland know a win would guarantee a first-place finish, while a draw would likely be enough due to their significant goal difference advantage.

They would even progress with a defeat if Estonia fail to beat Bulgaria, but they will certainly fancy their chances of taking all three points, considering they are currently League C's highest scorers and have recorded shutouts in each of their last five matches.

Luxembourg are competing in their fourth consecutive League C campaign, knowing they will remain in the third tier no matter the result in Monday's trip to the Icelandic capital.

That is because they are six points adrift of the top two after each of their last four matches since beating Bulgaria 2-1 on matchday one.

In fact, they have failed to trouble the scorers in each of those four defeats, including another goal-shy display in Friday's narrow 1-0 home loss against Estonia, leaving them one point behind third-placed Bulgaria.

That result made it three consecutive home losses without troubling the scorers since Luxembourg won 3-0 against Malta in the second leg of their Nations League relegation/promotion playoff tie in March.

As they head on their travels for Monday's fixture, Jeff Strasser's side can take confidence from the fact they have won three of their last four away internationals, although their most recent away outing resulted in a 1-0 defeat against Estonia.

If they were to win on Monday, it would represent their first-ever away victory over Iceland and just their second head-to-head success at any venue after winning 3-1 in a European Championship qualifier in September 2023.

Iceland will be unable to call upon Stefan Teitur Thordarson and Kristall Mani Ingason, who were forced in the first half against Bulgaria.

Hordur Magnusson replaced Thordarson in the ninth minute in Plovdiv, but he will miss Monday’s fixture through suspension after picking up his second yellow card of the league phase.

As a result of those absences, Gunnlaugsson has decided to call up Hjortur Hermannsson, Brynjar Ingi Bjarnason and Saevar Atli Magnusson.

As for the visitors, Omar Natami will serve a one-match ban after collecting his second yellow card of the league phase in the narrow loss to Estonia.

In positive news, Dirk Carlson is back from suspension and is expected to slot into central defence for Monday’s away fixture.

Enes Mahmutovic and Enzo dos Santos are also pushing for starting spots after coming off the bench to play over 30 minutes in Friday’s defeat.

Valdimarsson; Palsson, Gunnarsson, Gretarsson, Tomasson; Ellertsson, Johannesson, Haraldsson, Sigurdsson; Oskarsson, Gudjohnsen

Moris; Bohnert, Selimovic, Mahmutovic, Carlson; Olesen; V Thill, Dos Santos, Cruz, Kadamani; Dardari

Iceland will be full of confidence after thrashing Bulgaria 5-0 last time out, and we think they will produce another free-scoring display against a Luxembourg side that are low on confidence after four consecutive defeats.
