#1649. Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their new season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the new season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

Alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

More defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

That goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

Newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

Thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

Then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

Everton have played some quick one and two-touch football around the box in this game, and another move ends with George shooting over the bar. Everton are making their first change: Patterson off, replaced by Rohl.

The game is still finding its shape again after all those Newcastle changes, but Murphy did force a sharp save from Travers with a low shot from a tight angle.

He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

The players on for Newcastle are: Woltemade, Murphy, Willock, Barnes, Ramsey, Johnson, Steur, Pivas, Miley and Charlton.

It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

Everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

A sign of some Newcastle frustration there was Wissa kicks Tyrique George across the shins. A bit naughty that, may even have been worthy of VAR attention in a Premier League game.

The Senegalese sends Hornicek the wrong way and finds the corner. No chance it was a penalty in the first place though, thankfully this is not a competitive game.

This is very soft, there was not much of a challenge by Joelinton on Dewsbury-Hall, but the Everton midfielder goes down in the box and is awarded the penalty.

It really should be 2-0 to Everton, a high-class moving down their left with Armstrong dinking a pass to Barry. He squared to Ndiaye who was free as a bird in the middle, but his shot was too close to Hornicek.

Joelinton runs down a blind alley before lumping a pass out for an Everton throw, and then the Newcastle man fouls Barry. The big Brazilian still finding his legs and getting up to speed.

A moment to forget for both Newcastle centre-backs. Thiaw was bumped and unbalance by Barry, before Botman steps out of defence and kicks fresh air against the Everton forward. Great recovery from Lewis Hall, but the ball breaks for Armstrong, who feeds Barry and he finishes across Hornicek.

Ndiaye has had a quiet start to the game for Everton, but his jinking qualities were on display there to beat a couple of Newcastle defenders. Everton lose the ball in midfield, and Tarkowski makes a superb last-ditch tackle to deny Osula.

Half-hearted appeals for a penalty from Wissa, but Hayden Hackney did not do much wrong. Looks like we will be spared a first-half hydration break, despite it being a sultry evening.

Osula skips through a couple of challenges at the edge of the area but fails to pick a pass in the box. Bazoumana Touré has looked lively for Newcastle on their left flank, and Bamba has done well for them in midfield.

Everton shake themselves into life as an attacking force. Cracking cross from Patterson into the box and Dewsbury-Hall’s run had gone untracked, but he was just stretching and could not generate enough power to beat Hornicek.

Good save from Travers to deny Elanga, but it was Mykolenko who made a hash of things in the box. The left back simply fell over the ball under no pressure. Newcastle the sharper of the two teams so far.

Joelinton feeds Bamba down the left wing for Newcastle who delivers a cross into the penalty area. Keane can only direct his defensive header back towards the penalty spot, but Wissa volleyed over with a first-time hit. Decent chance.

Thierno Barry makes it stick and proves a strong outlet for Everton. Botman brings him down at the expense of a free-kick just beyond the halfway line. Then Wissa drives into the penalty area for Newcastle after a one-two but he fouls Patterson.

Newcastle, playing in their lilac away kit, are the team trying to take the initiative with the ball, but Everton are quite happy staying compact and absorbing pressure. Elanga’s corner delivery is promising, but Osula does not connect cleanly at the back post.

Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

Bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

We know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Big Dunc and Moyes catch up pre-match! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/Jh4APHOZvX

A word that keeps being used about Jaissle is “special”. Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton, Bamba; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula

Newcastle subs: Gillespie, Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Johnson, M Miley, Finneran, Ramsey, Steur, Willock, J Murphy, Barnes, Neave, Woltemade

Your Mags at Murrayfield! ✊ pic.twitter.com/rDXpn0MqCg

Everton XI: Travers; Patterson, Tarkowski, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Deswbury-Hall, Armstrong, Ndiaye; George, Barry

Here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#1648. Students need AI-free spaces to learn core skills

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In his World view, Marc Schmitt argues that if universities teach students to argue with artificial-intelligence systems and assess their debating skills, and if developers offer learning modes, then students will use such tools as a sparring partner rather than as an oracle (see Nature 657, 575; 2026). #1647. Arsenal-linked Antonio Nusa channels 'inner Ronaldinho' as Norwegian media hail RB Leipzig star

By Ben Knapton | 15 Nov 2026 09:45

Arsenal-linked attacker Antonio Nusa sent tongues wagging once again with a standout performance in Norway's 3-1 UEFA Nations League victory over Wales on Saturday night.

The RB Leipzig protege has been linked with a £66m move to Arsenal in 2027, with sporting director Andrea Berta apparently accelerating his plans to bring Nusa to the Emirates Stadium.

The 21-year-old did his hopes of a marquee transfer no harm whatsoever in Norway's triumph against Wales, most notably opening the scoring on the stroke of the hour mark with a low strike from the edge of the area.

Nusa was a livewire all evening for Norway, having also registered four shots, drawn two fouls, completed nine progressive carries and created three chances at Ullevaal Stadium, triggering high praise from the Norwegian media in the process.

Nusa was awarded an 8/10 rating from Tipsbladet, who hailed the Leipzig winger for 'doing everything on his own' and being a 'constant moment of unrest' for Welsh defenders.

433 also gave Nusa an eight for being "Norway's biggest threat" on the night, as well as 'igniting the crowd' with his effervescent performance on the left-hand side.

VG, meanwhile, made an extremely bold claim, stating that Nusa brought out his 'inner Ronaldinho', reflecting on a moment when the Arsenal target took out several Wales players with a mazy dribble before being unable to find the target.

Aftenposten could not help but wax lyrical about Nusa either, labelling the 21-year-old the 'wizard' that fans came to see, and a player who strikes 'terror' into opposing defenders.

The Nusa love-in was not limited to Norwegian commentators, as Wales boss Craig Bellamy told the media after the game that he would put the Leipzig man in the top three or four players in the world in his position.

"If I was in one of the top three, four, five clubs in the world, I would have signed him," VG quotes Bellamy as saying. "If I had the money, of course, because he is going to be very expensive. But I would go all in for him.

"I think he is a very special player. Difficult to control. Physically absolutely enormous. In terms of wingers, I would put him among the three or four best players in the world in that area."

Norway's triumph leaves the Nordic nation third in League A Group 4 on six points from five games, three adrift of second-placed Denmark, whom they face in Tuesday's finale.

Victory for Norway in Copenhagen will guarantee a quarter-final place for Stale Solbakken's men, but failure to win will see them either qualify for the relegation playoffs or suffer an immediate demotion to League B.

Nusa now boasts 10 goals and 10 assists in 35 caps for Norway, while he has registered a striking six goals and eight assists in 15 matches for Leipzig in the 2026-27 season.

#1646. The little-known new face called up by England: Can you name the star brought in to replace Ezri Konsa?

Published: 05:58 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 12:26 EST, 10 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel has made a first-time England call-up to replace Ezri Konsa - but casual fans could be forgiven if they do not recognise the latest Three Lions addition.

He is not a widely-recognised face among the stars from the Premier League and other top European leagues in Tuchel's selection but James Hill, 24, has starred for Bournemouth in their eight-match winning run under Marco Rose this season.

The central defender, who started his career at Fleetwood Town, has enjoyed a dream few months: He married partner Tara Rose in June, welcomed his first child in August and has now had his maiden England call.

England announced today that Arsenal defender Konsa will not be in contention to face Croatia at Wembley on Thursday night - although he will be fit to potentially face Spain away on Sunday - and Hill has been called up in his place.

Hill has played for England's Under 20s and Under 21s but this is his first senior call. He was signed by Bournemouth for just £1.2million in 2022 - beating Sheffield United, Burnley, Leeds, Southampton, Tottenham and even Barcelona, who all checked on his progress.

Bournemouth's official X account posted today: 'Congratulations, Hilly. Our defender has earned a first senior @England call-up.'

James Hill - pictured with new wife Tara - has been called up to the latest England squad (Source: Instagram/james_hill_10)

Hill has starred for Bournemouth in their eight-match winning run under Marco Rose

Hill's route to the top is a fascinating one. He attended a trial day at Fleetwood as a 14-year-old and managed to impress them enough to earn place at their new academy.

Interestingly, Hill did not play for a football team of any kind before he was 10, simply kicking a ball around with friends and playing in the garden to hone his skills.

Blackpool opted against signing him after a trial and he was then dropped by Bolton after a short stint.

It proved to be a shrewd piece of talent identification from Fleetwood, with Hill later becoming the club's record sale, eclipsing the fee they received for Jamie Vardy.

And having signed for the Cherries in 2022, Hill has now established himself as a key member of Marco Rose's side.

He's played every minute of every Premier League match this season at the heart of the defence and clearly Tuchel has been impressed.

Speaking before his call-up, Hill said: 'It’s every kid’s dream, isn’t it? You grow up watching the Three Lions on TV, for the World Cup, the Euros. It’s one of the greatest honours you can have in football.'

Football is in the blood for Hill. His father, Matt, made more than 550 appearances in the Football League for the likes of Preston North End, Wolverhampton Wanderers, Sheffield United and Queens Park Rangers as a defender.

Hill played for England at age group level, pictured here kissing his now wife after a game

Hill's younger brother, Tyler, is also in the game, playing for Torquay United in National League South.

But Matt did not pressure his sons into the sport, with James previously telling the Times: 'He didn’t want me to feel as though it’s a job.

'He wanted me to feel like I’m wanting to be here because I love doing it. This is my passion. It brings me happiness. He wanted me to come to that conclusion, not for him to make that decision for me.'

Hill was a well-rounded sportsman and his secondary school did not even play football. Instead, he excelled as a fly-half for the rugby side and impressed as a javelin thrower.

He attributes his success as being aided by trying his hand at different disciplines and it is paying off in abundance having had to largely bide his time before earning a first-team spot under Andoni Iraola last term, with loans to Blackburn and Hearts helping him develop.

Hill's progress flew somewhat under the radar somewhat for many fans outside of Bournemouth and his career peak of an England call-up coincides with domestic bliss.

Having married Tara in the summer, they welcomed their daughter Edie two months later.

Hill, pictured, heading the ball away against Ipswich has become one of the best defenders in the Premier League

'Becoming a dad is one of the most special things I’ve ever experienced in my life,' he said. 'There isn’t a manual though, it’s just like, "Congratulations, you’ve got a baby". Then the door shuts! Hang on a minute. What am I supposed to do next? Is there a book for this? My wife has been absolutely incredible.'

He regularly shares pictures from both his professional and personal life on social media, putting wedding snaps alongside action shots of Bournemouth games.

Hill's England call-up will no doubt introduce him to a whole new audience previously unaware of the defender's capabilities, with only 34,000 Instagram followers at present.

The 24-year-old must now impress Tuchel enough to earn some game time when England play Croatia on Thursday in their next Nations League encounter.

#1645. Belgian journalist admits Sylla may be ‘more inclined’ to move to England: “His dream destination”

AC Milan have been heavily interested in Massire Sylla recently, but it seems they may struggle to sign him, let alone in January.

It’s no secret that Milan want to sign a central defender and whilst Goncalo Inacio is the leading name, he’s not the only one in the mix. Instead, there are several public names of interest and Sylla is one of them.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

First linked by Matteo Moretto, his name has become more popular in reports linking the Rossoneri to defenders and he seems like a concrete target for the January mercato. Yet, it seems like it will be difficult to bring him to San Siro.

Speaking to MilanNews, Het Nieuwsblad journalist Tjorven Messiaen looked at Massire Sylla and what his future had in store.

In Italy, there’s been talk of AC Milan’s interest in Sylla. What’s being said about him in Belgium?

“I saw that AC Milan have linked him with him. In Belgium, we discovered him through social media, and the USG hasn’t confirmed anything yet. It’s possible, however, that AC Milan has drawn attention to the boy, because he’s playing great football.

“His move to AC Milan is unlikely to materialise in January, however, as both Sylla and the club would be more inclined to listen to offers from the Premier League. He’s the kind of player who would be a perfect fit for the English league.”

What are his main strengths and best qualities?

“He’s young, he’s good in duels, he’s quick. He’s also very good at ball control. He’s a complete defender; he has the potential to become one of the best, and he’d be a perfect fit in the Premier League, which, among other things, is Sylla’s dream destination.”

What aspects of his game still need improvement?

“It’s hard to say, especially since his growth in recent months has been impressive. I’d say he needs to gain more experience, which will come simply by playing. So I don’t see many things he needs to improve to take the next step in his career.”

Do you think Union Saint-Gilloise (USG) would be willing to let him leave in January, or do you think any transfer discussions will be postponed until the summer?

“I don’t think USG will let him leave in January. The only possible scenario, which I don’t think will happen, but which is the only solution anyway, is for USG to sign him in January but keep him at least until the end of the season, especially since the club never sells its best players in January.

“I also think interested clubs could spend a lot of money, but Union won’t let him leave in January.”

Could you describe him in three adjectives?

“Quick, physical, and full of character, because he’s someone who always has problems when he has to make decisions.”

“Considering his development, I’d say Pacho. He came from nowhere in Belgium, developed, moved to Frankfurt, and then ended up at PSG. In Sylla’s case, I think he’ll go straight to the Premier League. He has everything it takes to be perfect for this league.”

He’s still very young. Do you think he’s ready to play for a big club in a big city like Milan?

“He’s still very young, but he’s humble, calm, and we mustn’t forget that he arrived last year, in January, from the Norwegian second division. He played very little last year, but he’s very strong mentally and has started this season as if he’s been playing with this team for years.

“I can’t imagine USG without Sylla today, especially since we’re talking about one of the best defenders in the league. At the end of the season, he’ll make a significant leap in his career, but in my opinion it won’t be AC ​​Milan because he’s waiting for the Premier League. And from what I know, several English clubs are already ready to make him a player.

“So AC Milan could give him a try, but it will require a big project and a lot of money.”

We shall have to see how January develops and whether he could be sold on the project. However, it certainly doesn’t bode well from these comments.

#1644. Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

Two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

After Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia shows great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

A few minutes after I said that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away quickly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

As you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

Moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

In last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

What will we learn from the “new Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

Unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

“I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

“No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”

PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

#1643. Israel vs Austria - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 15 Nov 2026 10:02

Austria have already wrapped up UEFA Nations League promotion before they face Israel in their final League B Group 3 fixture on Tuesday.

Set to meet in neutral Debrecen, Ralf Rangnick's men are confirmed in first place, while the Israelis are at risk of relegation to League C.

Beaten by Serbia in the playoffs last time around - which cost them promotion to Europe's top tier - Austria have made no mistake in this season's Nations League.

With one game to go, they are already assured of a place in League A for the next edition, having built an unassailable five-point lead at the top of Group 3.

First place was confirmed at the Raiffeisen Arena on Saturday night, when substitute Sasa Kalajdzic poked home from close range to secure victory over the Republic of Ireland.

Heading towards the final 10 minutes, the LASK Linz striker finally ended a stubborn resistance from Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher, who had kept the hosts at bay with a string of sharp saves.

Having reached the knockout phase at the World Cup, Rangnick's side were always favourites to prevail in Group 3, and they never looked back after winning both of their first two fixtures.

In September, they kicked off by beating 10-man Israel 3-1, with Kalajdzic netting one of two late goals in Linz.

While their opponents are ranked 23rd by FIFA, Israel sit 76th in the global list and they lie rock-bottom of Group 3 as things stand.

After dropping down from League A in the previous edition, with only one win from six, the Israelis are on course for back-to-back relegations.

Ran Ben Shimon's side will either finish third and enter the demotion/promotion playoffs against a League C nation, or suffer automatic relegation once again.

It could be a complex conclusion to the group on Tuesday evening, but the best chance for Israel to avoid last place is by beating Austria and seeing Kosovo win in Dublin.

After holding the latter to a goalless draw at the weekend, the Sky Blue and Whites trail Ireland by two points and Kosovo by three, so their fate is out of their own hands.

Given they are guaranteed top spot, Austria may decide to rotate, as Rangnick continues to build for the future without some familiar faces.

Marko Arnautovic retired from international football after the World Cup, captain David Alaba has not been selected after struggling for fitness at Udinese, while Marcel Sabitzer is taking a break.

One of the new guard, Carney Chukwuemeka previously withdrew with a hamstring injury, while Werder Bremen winger Marco Grull pulled out because of a calf problem.

Israel will be missing key defender Raz Shlomo, who must serve a suspension for accumulated bookings; Barcelona teenager Orian Goren is also unavailable due to a muscular issue.

Dor Peretz - who scored in a Qatar 2022 qualifier against Austria - should join Ajax forward Oscar Gloukh in support of a lone striker.

With just two international goals between them, Idan Gorno and Dor Turgeman are the main contenders to feature up front.

Da. Peretz; Dasa, Feingold, Nachimas, Stoinov, Revivo; Abada, Azoulay, Do. Peretz, Gloukh; Turgeman

Jungwirth; Posch, Svoboda, Affengruber, Prass; Seiwald, Laimer; Demir, Baumgartner, Schmid; Kalajdzic

Though they might take their foot off the gas with promotion secured, Austria are a class above their final Group 3 opponents.

Rangnick's side remain unbeaten in five games so far - while scoring at a rate of two goals per game - and they can finish with a flourish in Hungary.

#1642. England given 10% chance of Spain Nations League win as Ben White/Cole Palmer claim made

By Ben Knapton | 15 Nov 2026 10:43

Ahead of Sunday's UEFA Nations League battle between Spain and England, Sports Mole site coordinator Ben Knapton explains why the Three Lions only have a "10-15%" chance of topping the group and makes an intriguing claim over Ben White and Cole Palmer.

I'd give them a very slim chance. We know that any win will do because in the Nations League, head-to-head results take precedence over goal difference.

If England win by one goal, they're level with Spain on head-to-head points, head-to-head goal difference and head-to-head goals scored, so then overall goal difference takes precedence, where England are superior to Spain.

If they win by two or three goals, then they top the group as well.

It's quite hard to judge based on what we've seen in one game, especially because I think we're now at that point in the season where fatigue is building and domestic and European commitments are really ramping up, especially for Premier League players.

I think we saw a bit of that in England's performance against Croatia. Quite a few standout names, I wouldn't say they had off nights, but they were just OK.

Lewis Hall was a standout, and Morgan Rogers too, but there was no one I really thought, "Wow, that was a magnificent individual display."

A win against Croatia is still nothing really to be scoffed at, even if they're not the Croatia side that they used to be. But facing world champions Spain, it's not impossible, of course. Nothing is impossible in football, but it'd be a very slim chance for me.

There is one thing that England are better at than Spain recently; they've scored two or more goals in each of their last six games, while Spain have done it in each of their last five.

Although the last time Spain scored just the one goal was in the World Cup final, so I can't really get too big-headed on that front.

Spain are now unbeaten in 43 matches, they haven't lost in 32 months, so I'd be pretty shocked if England could get the job done.

It's going to be really interesting to see what Tuchel does team news wise, because we're hoping that he'll be boosted by as many as three returns for this game.

Lewis-Skelly was banned against Croatia, and he'll return here. Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence just trained individually before the Croatia game, but there's hope that they'll return. I would absolutely start Konsa over Quansah for this game.

It's going to be fascinating to see whether Ben White comes in at right-back. He was booed again last night when he came off the bench.

He previously came out and said that if people knew the full story, then they wouldn't boo him. Now I'm just thinking, if Cole Palmer comes back into the squad, is he going to get the same level of treatment?

It is not an identical situation to Ben White, pulling out for load management versus personal reasons, but that's one I'll be fascinated to see if he gets called up in March.

Interestingly, I have seen some criticism of Declan Rice in an England kit. With Arsenal, Arteta really plays to his strengths, dropping him in between the centre-backs, where he can play those line-breaking passes.

We don't really see that so often for England, so I've seen quite a few people saying if Alex Scott was in the squad, they would start him alongside Elliot Anderson.

Lewis-Skelly is another option now that he's back from his ban, but I think it'll be Rice and Anderson in the middle. It'll be the same front four, but I would give them maybe a 10 to 15% chance of getting the win they need to top the group.

#1641. Hearts boss Vrancken is playing with fire by turning the guns on his own players

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 12:17 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 12:26 EST, 10 November 2026

Not for the first time this season under Wouter Vrancken, Hearts suffered a complete and utter implosion as they were thrashed 5-2 at home to Falkirk last weekend.

This is a team who lost 6-0 to Sturm Graz over two legs in the Champions League qualifiers back at the start of the campaign.

A team who were then battered 6-1 away against Benfica in Lisbon in the Europa League qualifiers – and a team who were also thumped 7-1 against Celtic at Parkhead a few weeks ago.

Hearts also lost the derby to Hibs just over a week ago in the semi-finals of the Premier Sports Cup at Hampden.

Now comes an annihilation against Falkirk where Hearts were 4-0 down by half-time. What a shambolic way to lose a long unbeaten record at home.

Even accounting for what had gone before in some of those matches this season, what happened on Sunday at Tynecastle felt like a new low.

Hearts were a shambles. But what was even more alarming was the manager's inability to stop the bleeding and make any changes from the touchline.

All of which poses a very simple question. Have Hearts and Jamestown made a mistake with Vrancken? At the moment, he looks hopelessly one-dimensional.

But it was his post-match comments on Sunday afternoon which actually became even more alarming than the performance itself.

Wouter Vrancken was 'embarrassed' by Hearts' 5-2 home loss to Falkirk

Vrancken branded it 'embarrassing' and a 'disgrace'. He called his players 'childish' and basically insinuated that they lacked any spirit or character until the youngsters came off the bench.

In the midst of a horrendous injury crisis and with players dropping like flies, that is a very dangerous game for any manager to play. He threw them under a bus.

By publicly slaughtering his players like that during a time of adversity and when many of them are being asked to play out of position, he is playing with fire.

Those are the type of comments that could very easily lose a dressing room. His comments would have gone down like a lead balloon among the squad.

Hearts have had the best part of a dozen players missing through injury. Vrancken himself has branded it an injury crisis unlike any other he has experienced throughout his career.

But what is most curious in all of this is that Vrancken seems totally unwilling to engage in any self-reflection throughout all of this.

After the shellacking at Celtic Park a few weeks ago, he lamented the fact his team had made too many individual errors.

There was no acknowledgment that his system had set them up to fail. No acceptance that pressing Celtic man-for-man and leaving players one-v-one at the back was a huge part of the problem.

Since he arrived in the summer, Vrancken's preferred style of play has been front-foot attacking football. There have been times when it has clicked reasonably well.

When he had his key players fit, Hearts were a good watch. But when the guts of a full team were then ripped out due to injury, it has quickly disintegrated into chaos.

Continuing to demand the same high-pressing and attacking style of play without meaningful adjustment is not principled. It is naive, inflexible, and tactically illiterate.

When the structure collapses, as it did against Falkirk and in the 7-1 defeat at Celtic, the emphasis returns to individual mistakes rather than collective vulnerability created by the system itself.

It is a classic example of a manager publicly hanging his players out to dry rather than choosing to accept his own part in the wider failings.

Hearts are not in crisis yet. They still sit fourth in the table, just a point behind Falkirk. But this is a team who have clearly regressed from where they were last season.

Vrancken was hired on the basis that he could bring a more dynamic style of play and move the team forward from the platform left behind by Derek McInnes.

As written in these pages a few weeks ago after the defeat to Celtic, there is absolutely no prospect whatsoever of this Hearts team challenging for the title this time around.

The current combination of a horrendous injury list, a rigid tactical approach and increasingly pointed public criticism of the players is a dangerous mixture that threatens to undermine everything.

Scottish football's fixture congestion, the demands of European competition and the physical toll of the season have exposed the limits of Vrancken's one-dimensional plan.

Adaptation is not a betrayal of principles. It is a basic requirement of the job when circumstances change this dramatically.

The international break offers a brief window. A handful of bodies may return for Hearts' next fixture against Dundee at Dens Park.

The more important return would be a change in tone and a willingness to adapt the demands placed on those players left still standing.

Publicly branding his players as 'a disgrace' while refusing to acknowledge that the system itself is contributing to their vulnerability is a sure-fire way to get himself sacked.

Vrancken's Hearts squad has been ravaged by injuries this season

The manager is entitled to be angry. He is entitled to demand better. He is not entitled to ignore the context he is operating in or the effect his words will have on a group already stretched to breaking point.

Vrancken arrived with a clear identity and early promise. The test now is whether he can evolve that identity under pressure or whether he remains locked into one way of playing regardless of the resources available.

Hearts cannot afford the latter. Much more of this public slaughtering and the players will switch off. Vrancken will have lost them completely.

Players will run for a manager who shows understanding of their situation even while criticising their standards.

They will begin to switch off for one who appears to place the preservation of his methods above the protection of the group.

That is the risk Vrancken is running. It is a risk no manager in the middle of a crippling injury crisis can afford to take.

#1639. Jorge Jesus responds after Cristiano Ronaldo tribute ends in Portugal record defeat

By Naim Beneddra | 15 Nov 2026 10:52

Portugal's first home match since Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement was supposed to celebrate the end of an extraordinary era. Instead, a 4-1 defeat to Denmark produced the country's heaviest-ever home loss in competitive football and prompted a remarkably blunt response from Jorge Jesus about his former captain.

The Portuguese players walked onto the pitch in Braga wearing Ronaldo's iconic number seven shirt, while supporters unveiled a giant banner reading "Obrigado, Capitão" — "Thank you, Captain".

An additional tribute followed in the seventh minute, with Ronaldo's image appearing on the stadium screens as fans applauded the 41-year-old, who announced his international retirement on November 5.

By the final whistle, however, the atmosphere had changed dramatically. Some supporters had left the stadium, while others chanted Ronaldo's name as Denmark inflicted a humiliating defeat on the reigning Nations League champions.

Asked afterwards whether Portugal were missing their former captain, Jesus delivered a pointed response.

"How can I miss him when he's no longer with the national team? What is there to miss? Maybe just his company," the 72-year-old told reporters.

"He doesn't play anymore, he's not here and he's already decided his future."

The comments added another chapter to the strained relationship between Ronaldo and Jesus, whose disagreement over the forward's international role preceded his retirement.

The scale of Saturday's defeat becomes even more striking when placed alongside Portugal's history.

According to Portuguese statistics outlet Zerozero, the national team had never previously lost a competitive home fixture by three goals or more.

Portugal's last defeat by such a margin on home soil came on September 6, 2003, when Spain secured a 3-0 friendly victory in Guimaraes.

Ronaldo had made his senior international debut against Kazakhstan just 17 days earlier, at the age of 18.

It means Portugal's first home match following his retirement produced a result not seen on Portuguese soil since the opening weeks of his international career.

The last time Portugal had lost 4-1 at home was even earlier, against Finland in a friendly on March 27, 2002.

There is an important distinction: those previous defeats came in friendlies, whereas Denmark's victory was achieved in a competitive Nations League fixture.

The timing was particularly painful given the elaborate tribute organised by the Portuguese Football Federation to recognise Ronaldo's 23 years of international service.

The former Manchester United and Real Madrid forward ended his international career with 146 goals in 234 appearances, leaving behind records that underline the significance of his departure.

Saturday's celebrations were intended to recognise those achievements, but the match also exposed problems that Portugal must address without their former captain.

Rasmus Hojlund, another former Manchester United forward, scored twice for Denmark, while Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg and Joachim Andersen were also on target.

Bernardo Silva's stoppage-time goal merely reduced the margin of defeat.

Portugal had won their previous four Nations League matches under Jesus, including a 4-2 victory over Denmark in Copenhagen on October 1.

Six weeks later, the same opponents exposed serious weaknesses in the Portuguese defensive organisation.

Jesus refused to connect Ronaldo's absence directly with Saturday's result, insisting that the former captain had already made his decision regarding international football.

The Portuguese manager nevertheless acknowledged the significance of Ronaldo's contribution and understood why supporters were chanting his name.

He explained that fans would naturally remember everything Ronaldo had achieved over 23 years with the national team, while recognising that some had left the stadium because of their disappointment with the scoreline.

On the pitch, Jesus identified a more immediate explanation for the collapse.

Speaking at his post-match press conference, as reported by A Bola, the former Benfica manager admitted that his side had been unable to contain Denmark's attacking movements, particularly after half-time.

He pointed to failures throughout Portugal's defensive structure rather than blaming the back four alone.

The pressing, usually a defining feature of his teams, had been especially ineffective.

Jesus acknowledged that Portugal's players repeatedly arrived too late to challenge the Danish ball-carrier, allowing the visitors to move possession forward before pressure could be applied.

That failure left the defensive line exposed, with Denmark exploiting spaces between Portugal's defenders.

The manager also admitted that the result had forced him to reconsider his plans for Tuesday's final group fixture against Wales.

He had initially intended to give opportunities to several players in Cardiff, but Saturday's performance means he may now rely more heavily on those who helped Portugal win their opening four matches.

Despite the historic nature of the defeat, Jesus rejected the suggestion that his previous work should be called into question.

He reminded his players that Portugal remained top of Nations League Group A4 and still controlled their own position.

The Portuguese have 12 points, three more than Denmark, and have already secured their place in the quarter-finals.

However, the Danes now hold the head-to-head advantage following Saturday's result and could overtake Portugal if they defeat Norway and Jesus's side lose to Wales.

A draw in Cardiff would be enough for Portugal to finish first.

Jesus therefore faces an immediate challenge: restoring the defensive discipline that disappeared against Denmark while preparing a team beginning life without its most influential international figure.

The Ronaldo tributes were meant to mark the end of one chapter in Portuguese football. Saturday's result has ensured that the beginning of the next will face considerable scrutiny.

#1638. Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward quickly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

You would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

Bottom left. Manchester United win the Boyle Sports Cup.

Smacks it even higher into the top right.

Some sealion ball juggling from Mazraoui involving foot, thigh and head, gets him past Justin on the right  but Gnonto heads away his cross.

Seven Manchester United changes: Mee, Tielmans, Shaw, Bruno Fernandes, Jack Fletcher, Matheus Cunha and Mazraoui incoming for Dalot, Lammens, Amass, Mbeumo, Diallo, Zirkzee and Tyler Fletcher.

Anyway, we are underway in the second period and the one change the majority of the stadium wants to be see is the introduction of Bruno Fernandes. Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have new signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

#1637. Alisson, 34, reveals he wants to STAY at Liverpool after rolling back the years against Crystal Palace... but is extending the goalkeeper's contract the right call, asks LEWIS STEELE

Published: 07:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 13:09 EST, 10 November 2026

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker insists he wants to stay at the club after his contract expires at the end of this season.

The Brazilian, now 34, put in a throwback performance in the Reds’ win at Crystal Palace on Sunday with some fine stops to keep his side in the game at 0-0 before the big-money attackers did their job at the other end.

It came after a period where Alisson has been questioned by fans for a string of errors in what is his final contracted year at the club. And the No1 has now opened up on his future for the first time.

Asked if he wants to stay beyond the end of the season, Alisson said: ‘Yes, in my mind. I’m focused on playing every game but in my mind I’m happy to stay. You know, that depends on a lot of aspects and different situations.

‘But my will is to stay. I’m happy here, my family is happy here. I’m still hungry for titles and for delivering good performances. I still want to play at the top level for as long as I can. So that’s my thinking on that.’

Alisson later added that his agent has held talks with the club over a new deal.

The 34-year-old keeper will spend the next week resting after not being called up by Brazil for the second straight international window

The keeper will spend the next week resting after not being called up by Brazil for the second straight international window, which he admits is a decision taken somewhat beyond his will.

He said: ‘It is beneficial (not going), for sure. You have to use it right because you have a lot of time so if you don’t train, if you don’t prepare, time goes really quick and you need to stay sharp.

‘It’s not that I will sit on the couch for a week and then come back training. I still have to work hard but in my mind I can use the time to relax and be more with my family.

‘It’s a little bit against my will. What I always want is to be with the national team but I understand this is what I have at the moment and I will use this time and take the benefit from the rest.’

Should Liverpool continue in Alisson wonderland?

It is tempting to just say ‘yes’ and end this debate there.

Alisson is still the best goalkeeper Liverpool have on their books and, even though he is maybe not as solid as he once was, the 34-year-old remains one of the best goalkeepers in the world.

Last summer, he flirted with the idea of leaving and seriously considered a move to Juventus. Alisson speaks fluent Italian from his time at AS Roma and held talks with the Turin club over a return.

But Liverpool triggered a clause in his deal to extend his stay by a year. With several big names leaving such as Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson, Ibrahima Konate and Curtis Jones, the club did not want another experienced head to depart and leave a leadership vacuum.

They have also spent the last three years succession planning for Alisson’s long-term replacement and have signed a number of goalkeepers for more than £60million combined.

Giorgi Mamardashvili is the most obvious in the pecking order. He has had mixed reviews with fans but the Georgian is appreciated more internally than maybe externally. The club believes he has several levels left to step up.

Lucca Brughmans will join from Belgian side Genk after a £28.3million deal was struck. Liverpool genuinely think he is the best goalkeeper on the market and they fought off stiff competition from Real Madrid to sign him.

Liverpool think Lucca Brughmans - who will join them from Belgian side Genk - is the best goalkeeper on the market and they fought off stiff competition from Real Madrid to sign him

They have also signed highly-rated Armin Pecsi and England youth goalkeeper Zach Trinder from Wolves.

Clearly, the post-Alisson future is sorted, with some of them tipped to go far in the game. But are any of them better than Alisson now? No. Will any of them be better next season? No.

Alisson missed 54 games across the previous two seasons with injury and illness, according to Transfermarkt, but his omission from Brazil camps and a specialised pre-season programme mean the keeper seems to have put his issues behind him. Touch wood.

For that reason, a one-year extension makes sense – for both Alisson and 35-year-old captain Virgil van Dijk. The club will have to face up to a future without both of their defensive stalwarts but, for now, they remain the best in class.

#1636. Cardinale says MSE will give Milan ‘financial muscle’ and reiterates: “I will never sell”

Gerry Cardinale has commented on the launch of AC Milan’s new holding company, Milan Sports & Entertainment (MSE), stating that he will never sell the club.

Yesterday, it was confirmed that RedBird had launched the new holding company to ‘consolidate RedBird’s Milan-based investments in sports, infrastructure, and entertainment’. From the new stadium to the NBA Europa project, there are big plans for the company.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Brett Yormark has been appointed as the CEO of MSE after impressing as the Commissioner of the Big 12 Conference (college sports), labelling it ‘an honour’ to get the position. It doesn’t mean that we will see less of Cardinale though, quite the opposite.

In an interview with Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Cardinale outlined exactly what he wants to achieve with MSE and explained why he will never sell the club. Silvio Berlusconi 2.0, as he calls it, with the goal of taking Milan back to the very top.

Cardinale, what benefits will AC Milan gain from the holding company?

“The driving force behind deals like this is to provide AC Milan with the financial muscle needed to compete in the transfer market and secure the best players in the world.

“I will transform the club’s financial profile with the resources that will come from the stadium, the San Donato Arena, and the other activities we are working on with NBA Europe.

“I’m doing everything I can to ensure that, when we want a player, no one can tell me, ‘You can’t sign him because you can’t afford him.’ Currently, only Premier League clubs are able to invest such sums and secure top players.

“If I want to bring AC Milan back to the top of European competition, not just in Italy, we need to figure out how to compete with the world’s top clubs.”

This project confirms that your commitment to Milan is long-term…

“Yes. I will never sell AC Milan. Never. And this is a project to get them back to winning ways. I’m not willing to tolerate it taking a long time to achieve this. I want to do it as soon as possible. We’ll see how quickly…

“My goal is to consistently win Scudetti and, of course, return to the Champions League. Milan Sports & Entertainment represents the foundation to make all this possible.”

The connection with Milan deserves a separate mention: RedBird and the city are now even more connected…

“This is the legacy we will leave in Milan. The stadium, obviously, represents a huge legacy that will transform our financial profile, but then there’s also the San Donato development project and the rest.

“If we want AC Milan to become great again, we need to close the revenue gap with the Premier League clubs. When I bought the club four years ago, I used the expression ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ and no one understood what I meant. Now perhaps we are starting to see it.”

“Everyone thought I was making an arrogant, self-centred comparison between me and Berlusconi, but that wasn’t my point. What I was trying to explain was that, just as Berlusconi transformed AC Milan and Serie A, we want to be able, through our ownership, to lead the club into a new era.

“We need to do it in the same way Berlusconi did, albeit in a modern way. I’m used to working a certain way because that’s how I do things, at the highest levels worldwide and in America.”

Could your “recipe” also be valid for Serie A?

“Of course, even for Serie A. In my opinion, it wouldn’t have been a good deal to sell 30% of the league’s international TV rights when JP Morgan made that offer. That’s not how Serie A can return to the top of Europe.

“It needs to be done through business planning and by creating every opportunity to generate new revenue. Like we will do with Milan Sports & Entertainment.

“We will be the first to build a stadium since 2011, and that’s a huge achievement. I started working on it when I bought AC Milan, and finally… the right time has arrived.”

Do you think others will follow you on this path?

“No. Some may do it, others may not. We know what it takes to innovate and change. To avoid continuing to practice Einstein’s definition of insanity, according to which everyone wants a different outcome, but doesn’t want to do anything different to get it.”

How long do you think it will take to complete the other projects that will be part of the new holding company?

“I think the NBA is negotiating with the Euroleague, but one way or another, if they can’t reach an agreement, NBA Europe will still launch. Perhaps the first batch of new franchises for Europe will be announced at the end of the year or in early 2027.

“We will see when that happens… We own the land in San Donato, and if I’m granted the Milan franchise, I will be able to start construction fairly quickly because we already have planning permission for a 20,000-seat arena.

“We will also continue to explore opportunities and hold discussions within the tennis world and to organise a tournament in Milan. Finally, we are already making progress in building and launching a hospitality and facility management company.”

Does your plan include organising and managing hospitality services for other clubs’ stadiums as well, not just the new San Siro?

“Yes, the model is the company I created in 2009, called Legends Hospitality. I created it with the New York Yankees and the Dallas Cowboys. Now that company is worth several billion dollars.

“We not only sell premium seats, suites, merchandise, and hospitality, food, and beverage services for Yankee Stadium and Cowboys Stadium, but also for other clubs. I would like to adopt the same model here, probably in partnership with another club.”

Not many football clubs in the world have established an organisation like the one you are leading…

“Exactly. My ambition is to compete with the best clubs in the world. I want to do so thanks to my global vision of the world of sports and entertainment.

“There aren’t many multi-sports platforms in the world that also own some of their own facilities, and we want to add AC Milan to that list. To compete with them and then be better.”

In an effort to generate new revenue, are you also considering a tour for AC Milan next summer? Will that still be Australia or the United States?

“We have already discussed it with Amorim, and I will just tell you that if we play friendlies abroad, they will be in the United States next summer. If we do… We haven’t decided yet, and the decision will be up to Ruben.

“It will depend on what’s best for the team: playing friendlies abroad must add value to the group, not bring in a couple of million for the club. Those extra two million will no longer be our goal, as they were under the previous management. That won’t happen again under this ownership.

“Everything we organise in terms of friendlies will be carefully considered with our coach. Every move. And we won’t participate in tours organised by others. We put our players first. We want to help them prepare well to win. That’s our goal, and we aim to achieve it as soon as possible.”
